chunks: And it is narrated from al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurrah al-Samandī that he said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me, “Do you know who the miser is?” I said, “He is the stingy person.”

He said, “Avarice is more severe than stinginess. Indeed, the stingy person withholds what is in his hand, while the avaricious person is avaricious regarding what is in the hands of people and regarding what is in his own hand, such that he does not see anything in the hands of people except that he wishes it would be his, by lawful and unlawful means, and he is not content with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has provided him.”

key_terms.ٱلشَّحِيحُ: the avaricious person; one who covets both his own possessions and those of others
key_terms.ٱلشُّحُّ: avarice or greedy possessiveness, a more severe moral vice than mere stinginess
key_terms.ٱلْبَخِيلُ: the stingy person; one who withholds what he possesses
key_terms.ٱلْبُخْلِ: stinginess; withholding one’s own wealth or resources

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between stinginess and avarice in the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between ordinary stinginess and the deeper vice of avarice. It teaches that shuhh is worse because it combines withholding one’s own wealth, coveting what others possess, and lacking contentment with Allah’s provision.
